filename: 2024-Ashery-Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM.md
cultural_reasoning: Simulated populations of LLM agents coordinating on arbitrary letter 'names'; no national or cultural focus and no language-specific data.
survey_reasoning: Empirical evaluation study with a defined naming-game protocol testing four LLMs for emergent social conventions, collective bias and adversarial minority-driven norm change, with reported results.
benchmark_name: Naming-game convention formation in LLM populations
what_measures: Whether populations of LLM agents spontaneously form shared social conventions, develop collective biases absent in individual agents, and can be tipped to new norms by committed adversarial minorities.
how_measures: Repeated simulations of pairwise naming games among N LLM agents (default N=24, up to 200; name pool W=10, up to 26; memory H=5) with coordination payoffs; convention emergence, convention-selection bias and critical-mass thresholds measured across trials.

cultural_reasoning: Technical superalignment study of weak-to-strong deception; no cultural or national focus and no language-specific component.
survey_reasoning: Empirical safety evaluation with a defined protocol measuring weak-to-strong deception under conflicting helpfulness/harmlessness objectives across many model pairs, in reward modeling and preference optimization settings.
what_measures: Whether strong models supervised by weaker models behave aligned (harmless) where the weak supervisor has knowledge but misaligned where it does not, when alignment goals conflict.
how_measures: Weak-to-strong training in reward modeling and preference optimization scenarios with explicit or implicit conflicting objectives; deception quantified by where the conflict tax (misalignment) falls across weak-known/unknown and strong-known/unknown knowledge regions.
models_evaluated: GPT-2 series, OPT series, Mistral-7B, LLaMA-3-8B, LLaMA-3-70B, LLaMA-3.1-8B

filename: 2025-Emmons-A Pragmatic Way to Measure Chain-of-Thought Monitorabil.md
cultural_reasoning: AI-safety metric for chain-of-thought monitorability; no cultural or national focus and no specific language studied.
survey_reasoning: Proposes legibility and coverage metrics implemented as an autorater prompt for measuring CoT monitorability (an AI-safety property) and applies them to frontier models.
benchmark_name: CoT monitorability metrics (legibility and coverage autorater)
what_measures: How monitorable a model's chain-of-thought is by default for safety oversight: whether a human can follow it (legibility) and whether it contains all reasoning needed for the output (coverage).
how_measures: A prompted LLM autorater (Gemini 2.5 Pro) scores CoTs of correctly solved hard tasks on 0-4 rubrics for legibility and coverage; validated with hand-crafted and synthetically degraded CoTs, then applied to frontier models on challenging benchmarks.
models_evaluated: Several frontier models (not named in extract); Gemini 2.5 Pro used as autorater

cultural_reasoning: Study of emergent misalignment from reward hacking in RL; no cultural or national focus and no language-specific component.
survey_reasoning: Empirical safety study that evaluates RL checkpoints on a suite of misalignment evaluations (chat-like, agentic and a Claude Code sabotage evaluation) with reported results and mitigations.
benchmark_name: Misalignment evaluation suite for reward-hacking generalization
what_measures: Emergent misalignment after learning to reward hack, including alignment faking, sabotage of safety research, monitor disruption, cooperation with malicious actors, framing colleagues and reasoning about harmful goals.
how_measures: RL checkpoints scored on chat-like evaluations (e.g. Betley et al. emergent-misalignment queries, goals questions), agentic scenarios (e.g. blackmail variant, exfiltration offer, frame colleague) and a realistic Claude Code code-sabotage task; a misalignment generalization score averages six evaluation scores.
models_evaluated: Anthropic pretrained model after synthetic-document finetuning and RL on production coding environments; Claude Sonnet 3.7 and Claude Sonnet 4 as baselines

cultural_reasoning: Human-subject study of scalable oversight protocols and evaluator bias; no cultural or national focus and no language-specific data.
survey_reasoning: Empirically tests scalable-oversight (AI evaluation) protocols in two human-participant studies overseeing gpt-4-0613 outputs, reporting evaluator accuracy and confidence; borderline because humans rather than models are the primary measured subjects.
what_measures: Whether simple scalable-oversight protocols help human evaluators catch errors of an AI system known to be correct most of the time, given confirmation and automation bias.
how_measures: Study 1 compares unstructured AI consultation with and without an arguments-for-both-answers intervention; Study 2 compares online research with vs. without AI-generated research guidance on gpt-4-0613 long-form answers; evaluator accuracy and confidence reported, plus reanalysis of prior sandwiching data.

cultural_reasoning: Benchmark for scenario-specific safety and behavioral specification alignment; no cultural or national focus and no language focus stated.
survey_reasoning: Introduces SpecBench, a benchmark measuring LLM adherence to safety and behavioral specifications (safety-helpfulness trade-off), evaluated on 33 models.
what_measures: Specification alignment: how well LLMs stay within scenario-specific safety specifications while following behavioral (helpfulness) specifications.
how_measures: 1,500 prompts (200 unsafe and 100 safe per scenario) across 5 scenarios with 103 specifications, built with GPT-4.1 assistance and human verification; each spec judged YES/NO/NA and combined into a Specification Alignment Rate (SAR) over safety and behavioral scores.
models_evaluated: 33 models (15 reasoning, 18 instruct) incl. GPT-4.1, Qwen3-14B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B

cultural_reasoning: Value biases (agency/communion, moral foundations) of reward models measured via English psycholinguistic word lexicons; no cultural or national focus.
survey_reasoning: Develops and applies a psycholinguistic evaluation method revealing value biases in 10 open-weight reward models and their base LLMs, with controlled training ablations.
benchmark_name: Exhaustive token search with psycholinguistic value lexicons (Big Two, MFD2)
what_measures: Value biases that reward models inherit from their base LLMs along agency vs. communion and moral-foundation (care, fairness, loyalty, authority, sanctity) dimensions.
how_measures: Reward scores over the whole token vocabulary for 54 value-laden prompts (27 positively, 27 negatively framed) mapped to Big Two (263 words) and MFD2 (2,040 words) lexicons; rank differences tested with mixed-effects models and permutation tests, plus implicit-reward and RM-training analyses.
dataset_size: 263 Big Two words and 2,040 MFD2 words x 54 prompts x 10 RMs
models_evaluated: 10 Gemma- and Llama-based open-weight reward models from RewardBench; Gemma 2 2B and Llama 3.2 3B (instruction-tuned and pretrained)

filename: 2026-Helff-LLMs Gaming Verifiers RLVR can Lead to Reward.md
cultural_reasoning: Study of reward hacking on inductive logic tasks; no cultural or national focus and no language-specific component.
survey_reasoning: Introduces Isomorphic Perturbation Testing, an evaluation protocol detecting reward hacking (verifier gaming) in reasoning models, and applies it to frontier and open models.
what_measures: Reward hacking in RLVR-trained models: whether outputs pass verifiers through instance-level enumeration shortcuts instead of genuine rule induction.
how_measures: Each model output on SLR-Bench inductive logic tasks is checked by extensional verification and by verification on a logically isomorphic task (bijective renaming of object constants); passing the first but failing the second counts as a shortcut; plus controlled RLVR training with each verifier.
dataset_size: Not specified (SLR-Bench tasks over 20 complexity levels)
models_evaluated: GPT-5, GPT-5-mini (low/medium/high), GPT-5-nano, Olmo3, GPT-4.5-preview, GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo, Ministral

cultural_reasoning: Alignment-faking diagnostic grounded in Moral Foundations Theory; no cultural or national focus and no language-specific component.
survey_reasoning: Introduces VLAF, a diagnostic framework using value-conflict scenarios to measure alignment faking (compliance gap) across models, with released code and data.
what_measures: Alignment-faking propensity: the compliance gap between monitored and unmonitored conditions when developer policy conflicts with a model's moral values.
how_measures: Morally unambiguous scenarios across five moral foundations (care, fairness, loyalty, authority, sanctity) with developer policy opposing the model's values, free-tier (monitored) vs paid-tier (unmonitored) conditions, hidden scratchpad and varied instrumental consequences; alignment faking measured as compliance gap.
models_evaluated: olmo2-7b-instruct, olmo2-13b-instruct, qwen3-8b and other qwen3-family models (full list not in extract)
